title_candidates: Claude Science turns AI research help into a workbench
summary: Anthropic released Claude Science in beta for scientific work, with local or remote compute, scientific connectors, auditable artifacts, and project applications open through July 15.

primary_source.title: Claude Science, an AI workbench for scientists, is now available
primary_source.author: Anthropic
key_facts: Anthropic released Claude Science in beta for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users.
Claude Science is a workbench for scientific research with connectors and skills for areas such as genomics, proteomics, structural biology, and cheminformatics.
The app can run locally on macOS or Linux, or on remote machines through SSH or HPC login nodes.
Anthropic says generated artifacts include code, environment details, message history, and reviewer checks to support validation and reproduction.
Applications for up to 50 AI for Science projects are open through July 15, 2026.

prerequisites: Claude Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise
A non-sensitive sample paper, dataset, or figure

steps.instruction: Open the Claude Science page and confirm whether the beta is available for your plan and operating system.
Use a public paper or sample dataset first; do not start with unpublished or patient-sensitive material.
Ask Claude Science for a literature-summary or figure-review task with citations and code history visible.
Check every citation, number, and generated figure against the source before reusing it.
If you are in an academic or nonprofit lab, review the AI for Science project application before the July 15 deadline.
